entities.name: PMID:38265121
observations: Retrospective cohort of 179 children: stomal maturation was not independently associated with persistent tracheocutaneous fistula after adjustment for age at tracheostomy and tracheostomy duration; multivariable p=0.089.
Overall, 98/179 children developed TCF and 107/179 had matured stomas.

entities.name: PMID:27519875
observations: Retrospective pediatric series: persistent TCF occurred in 47/89 (53%) after maturation versus 20/44 (45%) without maturation; difference was not significant (P=0.44).
Nonrandomized groups may have differed in baseline risk.

entities.name: PMID:10605914
observations: Pediatric surgical series: TCF occurred in 6/59 (10.2%) decannulated patients with matured stomas versus 5/39 (12.8%) with nonmatured stomas.
The study concluded maturation did not increase TCF, but did not establish comparable groups.

entities.name: Stomal maturation and TCF
observations: Across three retrospective pediatric comparative series, surgical stomal maturation was not shown to increase persistent tracheocutaneous fistula rates.
The strongest adjusted study found no independent maturation effect after accounting for age and duration.

entities.name: Duration and TCF risk
observations: In children, longer tracheostomy duration was more consistently associated with persistent TCF than stomal maturation; dependence exceeding 24 months versus less than 12 months had RR 2.5217, P<0.005.
Younger age at placement and tracheobronchomalacia were also reported predictors in a separate pediatric multivariable study.

entities.name: Adult evidence limitation
observations: Direct adult incidence studies comparing matured versus nonmatured stomas were not identified; adult evidence mainly concerns TCF repair and prolonged cannulation risk.
Therefore, the conclusion is stronger for pediatric populations than adults.
